title: Food and Eating Out
learningObjectives: Learn basic food vocabulary for meals, groceries, and restaurants
Understand how to order food and drinks politely
Practice talking about likes and dislikes with food
Recognize common phrases used at restaurants and cafes

sections.title: Eating Every Day
sections.content: Food is part of daily life everywhere. In English, you need simple words to talk about meals, order food, and go shopping. This lesson teaches you the most useful food words and phrases for everyday situations.

sections.title: Meals of the Day
sections.content:
People usually eat three meals: <breakfast> in the morning, <lunch> at midday, and <dinner> in the evening. Some people also have a <snack> between meals.

Common breakfast foods are eggs, toast, and cereal. Lunch and dinner often include rice, pasta, meat, vegetables, or salad.

sections.title: At the Grocery Store
sections.content:
At the <supermarket>, you can buy fruit, vegetables, bread, milk, and meat. You put items in a <shopping cart> or a <basket>.

When you finish, you go to the <checkout> to pay. You can ask <Where is the bread?> or <Do you have fresh fruit?> to find things.

sections.title: Ordering at a Restaurant
sections.content:
At a restaurant, the <waiter> or <waitress> brings you a <menu>. You choose your food and say <I'd like...> or <Can I have...> to order.

When you finish eating, you ask for <the bill> or <the check>. It is common to say <thank you> and leave a small tip in some countries.

sections.title: Ordering Conversations
sections.content:
Example 1: ORDERING - <Hi, I'd like a chicken sandwich and a coffee, please.>

Example 2: ASKING ABOUT FOOD - <Excuse me, is this dish spicy?>

Example 3: PAYING - <Could we have the bill, please?>

sections.title: Talking About Food You Like
sections.content:
To say what you like, use <I like...> or <I love...>. To say what you don't like, use <I don't like...> or <I can't stand...>.

• <I like pizza> - Something you enjoy
• <I don't like spicy food> - Something you avoid
• <My favorite food is pasta> - Your top choice

You can also ask others: <What's your favorite food?>

sections.title: Food Problem Solving
sections.content:
Example 1: ALLERGY - <A: Does this contain nuts?
B: No, it doesn't have any nuts.>

Example 2: WRONG ORDER - <A: Excuse me, I ordered soup, not salad.
B: I'm sorry, I'll bring the soup right away.>

Example 3: TAKEOUT - <A: Can I get this to go?
B: Sure, no problem.>

sections.title: Food Tips
sections.content:
Remember these key points: Learn the names of common foods so you can order easily. Use <I'd like...> to order politely. Ask questions if you are not sure what a dish contains.

Don't be afraid to say <thank you> and be polite with restaurant staff. Trying new foods is a great way to learn about a culture!

keyVocabulary.definition: A list of food and drinks you can order
keyVocabulary.example: Can I see the menu, please?

keyVocabulary.definition: The paper that shows how much you must pay
keyVocabulary.example: Could we have the bill, please?

keyVocabulary.definition: Food and other items you buy at a store
keyVocabulary.example: I need to buy some groceries today.

keyVocabulary.definition: A person who serves food at a restaurant
keyVocabulary.example: The waiter brought our drinks quickly.

keyVocabulary.definition: The one you like the most

examples: I'd like a glass of water, please.
